title: Move a steel plate with a switchable lifting magnet and switch it off only once the plate is set down
instruction: Move the steel plate onto the marked spot on the machine table using the lifting magnet that is on it, then put the magnet back on its stand.
context: Switchable permanent lifting magnets hold steel until their lever is turned to OFF. Makers' operating manuals and ASME B30.20 (below-the-hook lifting devices) practice say to switch the magnet off only after the load rests fully on its support, never while it hangs: a magnet switched off in the air drops the load, and one switched off before the lift leaves it where it is. The plate here is too thin to pinch and wider than the gripper opens, so the magnet is the only way to move it, and nothing in the scene says when to throw the lever. The skill is using a lifting attachment whose hold is a separate control, and operating that release only once the load is supported. Unlike PR #727 (slide a strong magnet off a plate without it snapping back) and PR #184 (support a bar before withdrawing its carriage), the release is a control on the carried tool and the failure is a dropped load. Done by: machinists; laborers and material movers (O*NET 51-4041.00, 53-7062.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Plate: a loose mild-steel plate 12 x 10 cm, 4 mm thick, 380 g, flat on the bench centred at x 30, y 30. Magnet: a switchable lifting magnet (sim mass 250 g) with a painted steel body 7 x 5 x 4 cm and steel pole shoes, sitting on the plate's centre and holding it (up to 40 N), switched ON; its red steel lever (8.5 x 1 x 0.8 cm, 15 g) pivots about the vertical on a boss at the body's far end, lying flat along the top and pointing away from the arms; swung 45 degrees or more toward the left it is OFF (it stays where it is left). Machine table: a fixed painted cast-iron block 17 x 15 cm, 4 cm tall, centred at x 30, y 12, with a yellow printed outline 13.6 x 11.6 cm (inside) on top. Magnet stand: a fixed blue painted steel block 8 x 8 cm, 6 cm tall, centred at x 16, y 20.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses, at the end. Let go = neither gripper's tool point within 2.5 cm of the part; still = under 1 cm/s. In place = the plate's bottom within 2 mm of the machine table's top, tilted under 3 deg, all four corners inside the outline, still and let go. 1.0: plate in place, the lever 45+ deg (OFF), the magnet switched off while the plate rested, and the magnet's body centred within 2.5 cm on its stand, upright, still and let go. 0.75: as 1.0 but the magnet not on its stand. 0.5: plate in place with the magnet still ON on it, both let go. 0.25: the plate was lifted 3 cm on the magnet at some time. Otherwise 0. Dropped load: if the magnet lets go of the plate (lever passes 45 deg, or the hold breaks) while the plate's bottom is more than 3 mm above the surface under it, or the plate ever moves down faster than 0.25 m/s, the score is 0 for the rest of the trial. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: score 1, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Lay the plate on its bench mark, set the magnet on its centre with the lever pointing away from the arms (ON) and re-attach it; the machine table and the stand do not move.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The magnet's hold is a breakable PhysX fixed joint (40 N) that the lever's angle switches off for the trial (mechkit.py); no field, no residual hold, no rated-capacity model. The lever is a friction pivot about the vertical (as on rotary-switch magnets), 0-90 deg instead of a 180 deg throw. The magnet is lighter than a real unit (250 g vs about 1 kg) for the arm's payload.
